items.title: 14.14 Strategies used to reduce air pollution

source_refs.note: Topic 14.14 with Figure 14.6, printed pages 317-318. The print announces five technologies and lists four.

blocks.text: A variety of technologies is used to reduce air pollution and improve air quality. The following are used to control emissions of air pollutants.

items: Catalytic converter: vehicle engines emit oxides of nitrogen, CO and unburnt hydrocarbons; most cars have catalytic converters that convert these to harmless substances: CO is oxidised to CO2, NOx is reduced to N2, and unburnt hydrocarbons are converted to CO2 and H2O.

Diesel particulate filter (DPF): fitted in modern diesel engines to reduce the emission of harmful particulate matter; its primary function is to capture and store the soot particles from the exhaust gases.

Selective catalytic reduction (SCR): used in diesel engines to remove pollutants from the exhaust; it reduces NOx to N2 and oxidises CO and hydrocarbons to CO2 and water vapour using catalysts such as TiO2 and zeolites (Figure 14.6).
Scrubbers: control a wide range of pollutants including particulate matter, SO2, HCl, NH3 and VOCs; they use liquids such as water to remove SO2 and PM from industrial exhaust gases.

blocks.alt: Exhaust after-treatment line. From the Engine, an arrow carries NOx, CO, HC and PM into the Oxidation Catalyst, then a narrow pipe where a blue urea line enters at the Urea Dosing System (a green cone), then a wide can holding the Urea SCR block and the NH3 Oxidate Catalyst block. An arrow leaves with N2, CO2, H2O and PM.
